newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN M2 MONEY SUPPLY UP 12.6 PCT IN FEB.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN M2 MONEY SUPPLY UP 12.6 PCT IN FEB.

text.p: Romania's M2 money supply rose by 12.6 percent in February after a 10 percent growth in the previous month, pushed by a strong increase in residents' hard currency deposits, central bank (BNR) data showed on Thursday.
M2, which is Romania's measure of broad money supply, was 37.8 trillion lei at end-February, or 99.98 percent up year-on- year, BNR data showed.
Higher inflation triggered heavy dollar hoarding, with residents' hard currency deposits going up to $1.94 billion at end-February from $1.83 billion in January.
Romania's monthly inflation surged to 18.8 percent in February after fuel, energy and food price liberalisation, while the local leu currency dipped to about 9,000 to the dollar in mid-February.
The leu, which started to recover last month on the back of tighter monetary policies, now trades at about 6,800.

The M1 narrow money, which includes currency outside banks and demand deposits, slipped to 8.9 trillion lei in February from January's 9.7 trillion, with demand deposits slipping some 13.4 percent to 4.5 trillion lei.
Cash in circulation was almost flat at 4.4 trillion lei in February, when household savings rose by 6.9 percent to 10 trillion lei.
